A cache key is the index entry [Cache](/en/documentation/platform/applications/cache/) stores an object under. Azion builds it from the request: the scheme, the host, the path, and the variations that a cache setting or [Image Processor](/en/documentation/platform/applications/image-processor/) adds. A request whose key matches a valid stored object is answered with that object. Otherwise the origin or a [Function](/en/documentation/platform/functions/) builds the response, and Azion can store that response under that key. For the lookup, refer to [Expiration and freshness](/en/documentation/platform/applications/cache/expiration-and-freshness/). For the fields that add variations, refer to [Cache settings](/en/documentation/platform/applications/cache/cache-settings/).

---

## Key format

The default key concatenates three elements of the request URI, in this order:

| Element | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Scheme | `https` |
| Host | `static.example.com` |
| Path | `/page/site.js` |

The query string is not part of the default key: `https://static.example.com/page/site.js?city=city&name=name` produces the same key as the URI without it. The query-string variation under Variations adds it.

The URI `https://static.example.com/page/site.js` produces the key `httpsstatic.example.com/page/site.js`. Keys are case sensitive: upper and lower case characters are distinct. When a cache setting turns a variation on, the key can end with the `@@` separator, as in `httpsstatic.example.com/page/site.js@@`. The table under Variations shows where each variation goes: the request method is a prefix, and the other variations follow `@@`, the query string included when its behavior is `allowlist` or `denylist`. Under `all`, the whole query string follows the path, before `@@`.

---

## Variations

A variation adds to the default key, so one URI can hold more than one object in the cache. The table lists what each variation adds and the key it produces.

| Variation | What it adds | Example key |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Complex request | The request method, prefixed to the key. A `GET` or `HEAD` request carries no prefix. | `optionshttpsstatic.example.com/page` |
| Query string | Under `allowlist` and `denylist`: `@@`, then `?` and the arguments the setting keeps. Under `all`: `?` and the whole query string, after the path and before `@@`. | `httpstatic.example.com/page@@?name=name`, `httpstatic.example.com/page?city=city&name=name@@` |
| Cookies | Under `allowlist` and `denylist`: `@@`, then each cookie name and value the setting keeps, followed by `;`. The empty variation, with no cookie value, is `@@;`. Under `all`, the whole `Cookie` header follows `@@` as it arrived, spaces included. | `httpwww.example.com/@@;`, `httpwww.example.com/@@user=user;` |
| Device group | `@@` and the name of the device group. | `httpwww.example.com/@@Mobile` |
| [Image Processor](/en/documentation/platform/applications/image-processor/) | The converted image format, at the end of the key with no separator. When the cache setting names `ims` in its query-string allowlist, the `ims` query string follows `@@`, and the format follows it. When the cache setting does not vary the key by query string, the `ims` value is not part of the key, so every size and processing of the path shares a key, and the first one stored answers every `ims` value. | `httpsstatic.example.com/static/images/image_1.jpg@@webp`, `httpsstatic.example.com/static/images/image_1.jpg@@?ims=880xwebp` |
| Large File Optimization | `@@bytes=<start>-<end>` for each fragment, so each fragment carries its own key. A file of 2,097,152 bytes produces two keys. | `httpsstatic.example.com/media/file.mp4@@bytes=0-1048575`, `httpsstatic.example.com/media/file.mp4@@bytes=1048576-2097151` |
| Cached `POST` | `@@` and the MD5 (Message Digest 5) hash of the request body, after the `post` prefix. A cached `OPTIONS` carries only the `options` prefix. | `posthttpsdynamic.example.com/path@@<md5-of-post-body>`, `optionshttpsdynamic.example.com/path` |

The query-string and cookie fields are case sensitive, so `user` and `User` are two variations. With `sort_enabled` on in the cache setting, `?name=name&city=city` and `?city=city&name=name` share one key, with the arguments in alphabetical order.

The query-string, cookie, device group, and request method variations make up Advanced Cache Key, a Feature of [Application Accelerator](/en/documentation/platform/applications/application-accelerator/). Each of them requires Application Accelerator on the Application. For what each behavior does to the key, refer to [Application Accelerator settings](/en/documentation/platform/applications/application-accelerator/settings/#cache-variation).

In Azion Console, these controls produce the variations, with the API field of each one in parentheses:

- **Cache vary by Method** (`cache_vary_by_method`) makes `POST` and `OPTIONS` responses cacheable.
- **Cache vary by Query String** (`cache_vary_by_querystring`) sets the query-string variation, with its **Behavior** and **Sort**.
- **Cache vary by Cookies** (`cache_vary_by_cookies`) sets the cookie variation.
- **Cache vary by Devices** (`cache_vary_by_devices`) sets the device group variation, for the groups defined in [Device Groups](/en/documentation/platform/applications/device-groups/).
- **Large file optimization** (`large_file_cache.enabled`) splits a large object into fragments, each with its own key.
- Image Processor, turned on in the Application (`modules.image_processor.enabled`), adds the format variation.

For the type and default of each field, refer to [Cache settings](/en/documentation/platform/applications/cache/cache-settings/).

---

## Debug headers

To read the status and the key of a response, send the request with the header `Pragma: azion-debug-cache`. The response carries several `x-cache-*` headers, and two of them hold the status and the key. `x-cache` holds the cache status, the IP address of the server that answered the request, and the protocol. `x-cache-key` holds the key:

```text
x-cache: MISS from 192.0.2.10 with HTTP/2.0
x-cache-key: httpsstatic.example.com/page/site.js
```

Under HTTP/2, the header names arrive in lower case. A `GET` or `HEAD` response that Azion does not store carries `-` in both headers while Application Accelerator is on; with it off, the same response reports `MISS`, with its key in `x-cache-key` and `x-cache-expires-in: 0`. A `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, or `OPTIONS` response that Azion does not store carries `-` either way. Consecutive requests for one path can each be answered by a different server, which `x-cache` names. For the procedure, refer to [Check the cache status of a response](/en/documentation/guides/application-performance/cache-and-purge/check-page-cache-time/).

---

## Cache status

The `x-cache` header opens with one of eight values. Each one names what Cache did with the request.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `HIT` | Valid, up-to-date content served from the cache of the data center that answered the request. The origin receives no request. |
| `MISS` | The content is not in the cache. Azion fetches it from the origin, and the response may be stored for later requests. |
| `EXPIRED` | The cached copy passed its time to live (TTL). When the origin responds, the response updates the copy for later requests. |
| `STALE` | Stale cache is on, the copy expired, and the origin failed to respond, so Azion serves the expired copy. |
| `UPDATING` | The copy expired, and Azion serves it while the content is updated from the origin. |
| `REVALIDATED` | Azion checked the copy against the origin with conditional headers, and it was still current, so the origin did not send it again. |
| `BYPASS` | The request went to the origin because a [Bypass Cache](/en/documentation/platform/applications/rules-engine/#bypass-cache) behavior applies. A response under that behavior can report `-` instead. |
| `-` | No status: Azion did not store the response. A `POST` reports it when caching for `POST` is off, and a `GET` or `HEAD` response that is not stored reports it while Application Accelerator is on. With Application Accelerator off, that `GET` or `HEAD` response reports `MISS` with `x-cache-expires-in: 0`. |

For more information on the `STALE` status, refer to [Expiration and freshness](/en/documentation/platform/applications/cache/expiration-and-freshness/).
